messages.content: use even though in a sentence about a walk i enjoyed in cold weather.
i enjoyed the walk even though the weather was cold.
does that mean the weather was not really cold?
no. both parts can be true. the weather was cold, and you enjoyed the walk.
what does even though add?
it says you enjoyed the walk although the cold could have made it hard to enjoy.
make that explanation shorter.
the cold did not stop you from having a walk you enjoyed.
now make a sentence about being tired but finishing a page.
i finished the page even though i was tired.
can i use it if i did not finish?
then change the first part. for example: i wanted to finish the page, but i was too tired. that gives a different story.
what if i was tired and still did finish?
then i finished the page even though i was tired keeps both of those facts.
only give the walk sentence again.
i enjoyed the walk even though the weather was cold.
in a made up town, the library is east of the school. the park is west of the school. is the park east of the library?
no. the park is west of the school, and the library is east of it, so the park is west of the library.
if i walk from the park to the school, which way do i go?
you go east to the school.
only tell me which way to go.
go east to the school.
now i go from the school to the library.
you keep going east.
can you know how many minutes that takes?
no. you gave which way the places are from each other, but not how far apart they are or how fast you walk.
give that explanation in fewer words.
i need how far it is and how fast you walk to know the time.
what if i start at the library and want the park?
you go west, with the school between the library and the park in the simple map you gave.
does this tell us about my real town?
no. you said it was a made up town. i should keep it as that example.
write a story about a child being told to choose one of the books. he should learn that this does not mean take every book.

a child came to the table where his aunt had put a few books. she said he could choose one of them to read that evening. he began carrying the whole group to his chair. she stopped him and asked how many he had heard in the request. he said he had heard books and thought the whole group was for him. she showed him the group, then held up one book. he looked at each story and chose the one he wanted most. the other books stayed on the table for another day. after reading, he put his choice back and told her which one he might try next.
why did the child take the whole group at first?
he heard books but did not use the detail one of them.
make that answer shorter.
he did not use the word one.
what did one of them ask him to do?
it asked him to choose one book from the group, not the whole group.
only give the part about what to choose.
choose one book from the group.
can you write the aunt request more clearly?
please choose just one book to read this evening. the rest can stay here.
what did he do with the chosen book after reading?
he put it back.
finish with him keeping the next choice open.
he looked at the other books before leaving, but did not choose one yet. another day, he could see what he wanted to read then.
i started a picture today. i like it, but i want to leave it until tomorrow before adding more.
you can give yourself time to look at it again. what part do you already like?
i like the house and the space around it. i am not sure whether to add people.
then you can leave that choice open. not adding them today does not mean you can never add them.
can you help me write a short note to myself about the choice?
i like the house and the space around it. tomorrow i can see whether i want to add people.
why not say i must add them tomorrow?
because you have not chosen that. tomorrow is a time to look again, not a rule that the picture needs people.
make that explanation shorter.
looking again does not mean you must add people.
what if i like it just as it is tomorrow?
then you can keep it as it is. waiting gives you time to choose, not a rule that you must change it.
make that reply shorter.
then you can keep it as it is.
only give the note again.
i like the house and the space around it. tomorrow i can see whether i want to add people.
can light be about what i see and also about how easy something is to carry?
yes. light from a window helps you see. a light container may be easy to carry without much work.
give one short sentence for each meaning.
the light helped me read. the container was light and easy to carry.
now explain the difference simply.
one sentence is about what helped you see. the other is about carrying an object.
can light also be part of a color?
yes. light can be used with a color, as in light blue. the meaning comes from how the word is used.
what if i only say it is light?
then someone may need context to know whether you mean color, what you can see, or how easy a thing is to carry.
ask a question to make the container meaning clear.
do you mean the container is easy to carry?
now only give the example about a window.
light from the window helped me read.
does that tell us the window is open?
no. light can come through a closed window too.
write a story about someone answering a question they think they heard, then asking for the real question.

a man was cleaning the kitchen when his daughter asked whether he had seen her book. he thought she had asked whether he wanted to read it, so he said he was busy. she did not understand his answer and asked again, saying that she could not find it. he stopped what he was doing and listened to the whole question. then he remembered seeing the book on the sofa. he told her where to look and said sorry for answering too soon. she found it there and returned to ask him about a sentence. this time, he asked her to show him the part before giving an answer.
why was i am busy not useful for the first question?
she wanted to know whether he had seen the book. she was not asking him to read with her at that moment.
what changed when she asked again?
he understood that she could not find the book and wanted to know where it was.
make that explanation shorter.
she needed the place of the book, not his help reading.
write his question before helping with the sentence later.
which part would you like me to look at?
why did that help?
it gave him the real part she needed, rather than having him choose a question she had not asked.
finish with them looking at the same sentence.
she put the page on the table and showed the line. he read it with her before answering.
i need one cup for tea now and one cup for water later. does that always mean i need two different cups?
no. if you can wash and use the same cup later, one cup can be used for tea now and water later.
make that explanation shorter.
you can use one cup now, wash it, and use it again later.
what if both drinks need to be on the table at the same moment?
then use two cups if each drink needs its own cup at that moment.
why is that different from one drink now and one later?
you cannot use the same cup for both drinks at once if each needs its own place. with one now and one later, you can wash and use the same cup again.
now i have three people who each need a cup of water together.
then you need three cups if each person must have their own at the same moment.
can you know i own three cups?
no. knowing how many you need does not tell us how many you already have.
i have only two. how many more do i need for three people?
one more cup.
only give that answer.
one more cup.
i cleaned the desk but not the whole room. help me tell my father what i did.
i cleaned the desk. the rest of the room is not finished yet.
can you make it sound like i am not saying the whole day went wrong?
i cleaned the desk today. there is more to do in the room, but that part is done.
what if i do not want to say the rest will be done tomorrow?
then do not add tomorrow. you can say what you finished without saying when you will do the rest.
make that explanation shorter.
say what is finished and leave the next day open.
now ask if he needs to use the desk.
i cleaned the desk today. do you need to use it?
does that say i moved his things without asking?
no. it says the desk is cleaned, but not how you did it or what happened to his things.
what if i want to say his book is still there?
i cleaned the desk today, and your book is still there. do you need to use the desk?
only give the first sentence without the question.
i cleaned the desk today, and your book is still there.
